chapters.title: Introduction
chapters.lead: This chapter shows what competitive programming is about, outlines the contents of the book, and discusses additional learning resources.
chapters.endText: You’ve met the two halves of competitive programming, the contests, the practice, the book, and a first problem with a subtle bug.

chapters.title: Programming Techniques
chapters.lead: C++ language features, recursive algorithms, and bit manipulation — the toolkit the rest of the book builds on.
chapters.endText: Language features, recursion, and bits — the three ideas the rest of the book leans on.

chapters.title: Efficiency
chapters.lead: How to estimate the running time of an algorithm before writing a line of code.
chapters.endText: Efficiency is a design constraint, not an afterthought.

chapters.title: Sorting and Searching
chapters.lead: Sorting as a problem-solving tool, and binary search on arrays and answer ranges.
chapters.endText: Sorting and binary search turn many hard problems into simple ones.

chapters.title: Data Structures
chapters.lead: Dynamic arrays, sets, maps, and the experiments that choose between them.
chapters.endText: Choosing a data structure is often the whole solution.

chapters.title: Dynamic Programming
chapters.lead: States, transitions, and the art of not solving the same subproblem twice.
chapters.endText: Dynamic programming trades memory for time by keeping what you have already computed.

chapters.title: Graph Algorithms
chapters.lead: Traversal, shortest paths, DAGs, successor graphs, and minimum spanning trees.
chapters.endText: Traversal, distances, and spanning trees cover a surprising share of contest problems.

chapters.title: Algorithm Design Topics
chapters.lead: Bit-parallel tricks, amortized analysis, and finding minima in clever ways.
chapters.endText: Bit-parallelism and amortized reasoning make the impossible merely fast.

chapters.title: Range Queries
chapters.lead: Prefix sums, sparse tables, segment trees, and Fenwick trees for static and dynamic ranges.
chapters.endText: Prefix sums and tree structures turn range queries into arithmetic.

chapters.title: Tree Algorithms
chapters.lead: Rooting, traversing, and querying trees — from LCA to centroid decomposition.
chapters.endText: Trees reward a traversal order and a little preprocessing.

chapters.title: Mathematics
chapters.lead: Number theory, combinatorics, matrices, probability, and games.
chapters.endText: Mathematics supplies both the tools and the shortcuts.

chapters.title: Advanced Graph Algorithms
chapters.lead: Strong connectivity, Eulerian and Hamiltonian paths, flows, and DFS trees.
chapters.endText: Connectivity, flows, and Eulerian paths are graph theory at full strength.

chapters.title: Geometry
chapters.lead: Points, lines, polygons, distances, and the sweep line.
chapters.endText: Geometry rewards exact predicates and a good sweep.

chapters.title: String Algorithms
chapters.lead: Hashing, the Z-algorithm, suffix arrays, and other string tools.
chapters.endText: Hashing and suffix structures make text searchable at scale.

chapters.title: Additional Topics
chapters.lead: Square-root decomposition, revisited segment trees, treaps, DP optimization, and a grab bag of techniques.
chapters.endText: Square roots, treaps, and DP optimizations round out the toolbox.
